text:
He withdraws into the depths of himself to think

how little he is. Perhaps he turns toward the tree

that suggests a gesture to him. After an hour,

it is rather the sand that influences him. Indolent,


he remembers an old love. He thinks himself well preserved

despite oblivion and the blood crowded

over his heart. He would not be so defenseless

if he had a friend: for example a pebble,


a dying bird, a warm hill.

First he closes one eye, then the other, scrutinizing himself

with fury. He discovers nothing fundamental


in his lungs or in his souls, which he takes off

one after another, just like his shirts.

All serenity seems an offense to him.

translation.title: Portrait of a Restless Man
translation.editorial_note: The odd plural souls is retained because the poem makes identity something removable and layered.
